facts.statement: The holotype of Liubangosaurus consists of five articulated middle-caudal dorsal vertebrae collected from the Xinlong Formation in Guangxi Province.
facts.quote: Liubangosaurus is known from the holotype NHMG 8152, five complete and articulated middle-caudal dorsal vertebrae that were collected from the Xinlong Formation in Fusui County, Guangxi Province.

facts.statement: Sauropod remains were first discovered at the Liubang Quarry in 2001 near Nanning in southern China.
facts.quote: Sauropod remains were first discovered at the Liubang Quarry in 2001, near the village of the same name (Liubang) which is near the city of Nanning in the Guangxi Province of southern China.

facts.statement: Liubangosaurus was formally described and named in 2010 by Mo Jinyou, Xu Xing, and Eric Buffetaut.
facts.quote: It was fully described and named in 2010 by Mo Jinyou, Xu Xing, and Eric Buffetaut.

facts.statement: The largest vertebra in the holotype, the fifth dorsal, measures 710 mm in total height.
facts.quote: The largest of these vertebrae (the fifth dorsal) has a total height of 710 mm.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated the full size of Liubangosaurus to be 26 meters long, 5.4 meters tall at the shoulder, and weighing 26 tons.
facts.quote: Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larramendi estimated its full size as being 26 m long, 5.4 m tall at the shoulder, and 26 tons

facts.statement: Liubangosaurus lived in a wetland environment during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The depositional environment consisted of various types of wetlands, which is reflected in the fossils that have been discovered in the area.

facts.statement: While originally classified only as an eusauropod, later analysis placed Liubangosaurus within the advanced group Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Originalmente solo se lo pudo clasificar hasta Eusauropoda, pero en 2013 Mannion et al., lo colocaron en la más avanzada Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Liubangosaurus may be closely related to the Late Jurassic genus Haplocanthosaurus, but noted this assignment is tentative due to the fragmentary fossil evidence.
facts.quote: They suggested that it may be a close relative of the Late Jurassic genus Haplocanthosaurus, however they also caution that this assignment is very tentative due to the fragmentary nature of the holotype.

facts.statement: The fragmentary nature of Liubangosaurus fossils has complicated scientific determinations of its phylogenetic relationships.
facts.quote: The fragmentary nature of Liubangosaurus has served to complicate determinations of its phylogenetic affinities.

facts.statement: Liubangosaurus lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Liubangosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Liubangosaurus (meaning "Liubang lizard", after Liubang village, the holotype locality) is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now China.

rejected.quote: In particular, the vertebrae have a very distinctive "Y-shape" when viewed along their transverse plane.
